thread.title: Appaloosa ups investments in Micron, Facebook, Apple, adds new bets in Caesars, MGM in 4th quarter - MarketWatch

author: Mark DeCambre
title: Appaloosa ups investments in Micron, Facebook, Apple, adds new bets in Caesars, MGM in 4th quarter - MarketWatch
text: Billionaire hedge-fund investor David Tepper's Appaloosa Management was a buyer of technology, energy and bank shares in the fourth quarter, according to a Wednesday regulatory filing. Between the end of the third and fourth quarter, Appaloosa boosted its stake in Bank of America Corp. BAC, +2.63% upping his position by 170% to 10.8 million shares. He also increased his stake in Apple Inc. AAPL, +1.84% raising that investment to 3.2 million shares and raising his stake in Micron Technology Inc. MU, +1.92% to 10.45 million shares, representing his largest holding according to WhaleWisdom.com. The hedge-fund luminary also lifted his position in Facebook Inc. FB, +3.68% by about 70% to 2.2 million shares, while adding to his holdings in the tech-heavy PowerShares QQQ Trust Series 1 QQQ, +1.87% to 4.3 million shares. Meanwhile, Tepper took a long position in the exchange-traded Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF XLF, +2.38% purchasing $280 million worth, though the fund also sold call options in the ETF worth $35 million. Call options give the holder the right but not the obligation to buy an asset a set price and time. Appaloosa also made bullish bets in the energy-centered Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF XLE, +1.45% for $35 million. The investor was a buyer in gambling assets, with new stakes in Caesars Entertainment Corp. CZR, +4.49% about 5.86 million shares, and MGM Resorts International MGM, +3.95% where he picked up 2.3 million shares, from the end of the third quarter. Tepper notably divested his entire stake in Kinder Morgan Inc. KMI, +0.35% Chesapeake Energy Corp. CHK, +2.19% Whirlpool Corp. WHR, +0.60% and General Motors GM, +0.99% recent filings showed. Large investors are required to reveal their long equity holdings at the end of each quarter in filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
